2607.18029.title: Natural Language Access to Domain-Specific Metadata: A Reusable Framework for LLM Query Generation
2607.18029.paper_summary: Researchers need to answer ad-hoc questions about the contents of domain-specific archives but often lack the expertise to write structured queries on the metadata. We show that when domain vocabulary and semantics are captured in a well-designed Web Ontology Language (OWL) ontology, Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate accurate structured queries zero-shot, without fine-tuning, retrieval augmentation, or multi-agent orchestration. We present the Natural Language Knowledge Graph Query (NLKGQ) system, a framework and development process that enables natural language access to metadata in such archives. The framework includes a web interface that helps researchers pose natural language questions, which a domain-agnostic harness translates to SPARQL via an LLM and executes against a knowledge graph. The development process begins with capturing domain vocabulary and semantics in a formal OWL ontology. Domain-specific code then extracts metadata from archive sources and imports it into a knowledge graph defined by the ontology. Both are designed for reuse across domains. We demonstrate the system on metadata derived from a large-scale neuroimaging research archive, evaluating multiple LLMs and ontology representations. The best configurations achieve 100% accuracy on a competence and regression question set developed with domain experts. An ablation study across eight ontology representations reveals that readable entity names and semantic annotations are the dominant factors in accuracy, more significant than model choice or prompt engineering. We also compare SPARQL to an auto-generated SQL database as query backends, showing that OWL's structural features provide a substantial advantage over SQL DDL for LLM-driven query generation. Our demonstration domain also requires local LLMs on modest institutional hardware to address privacy concerns for human subject data.
2607.18029.paper_summary_zh: 研究人員需要回答有關特定領域檔案內容的臨時問題，但往往缺乏撰寫結構化查詢的專業知識。我們顯示，當領域詞彙和語義在精心設計的網路本體語言（OWL）本體中被捕捉時，大型語言模型（LLMs）可以在零次學習的情況下生成準確的結構化查詢，而無需微調、檢索增強或多代理協調。我們提出了自然語言知識圖譜查詢（NLKGQ）系統，這是一個框架和開發過程，使研究人員能夠自然語言訪問這些檔案中的元數據。該框架包括一個網頁介面，幫助研究人員提出自然語言問題，這些問題通過一個與領域無關的工具轉換為SPARQL，並在知識圖譜上執行。開發過程始於在正式的OWL本體中捕捉領域詞彙和語義。然後，特定領域的代碼從檔案來源提取元數據，並將其導入由本體定義的知識圖譜。這兩者都旨在跨領域重用。我們在從大型神經影像研究檔案中衍生的元數據上演示了該系統，評估多個LLMs和本體表示。最佳配置在與領域專家共同開發的能力和回歸問題集上達到100%的準確率。對八個本體表示進行的消融研究顯示，可讀的實體名稱和語義註釋是準確性的主導因素，這比模型選擇或提示工程更為重要。我們還將SPARQL與自動生成的SQL數據庫作為查詢後端進行比較，顯示OWL的結構特徵在LLM驅動的查詢生成中提供了相對於SQL DDL的顯著優勢。我們的演示領域還需要在適度的機構硬體上運行本地LLMs，以解決人類受試者數據的隱私問題。
